title: Nvidia sells more than half of Nokia stake
html:
Nvidia has sold more than half of its stake in Finnish network vendor Nokia.

In a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing earlier this week, the chipset giant confirmed that it had sold more than half the stake in Nokia that it acquired last year.

Nvidia snapped up a 2.9 percent stake in Nokia as part of a $1 billion strategic investment to push AI networking.

The company acquired 166 million shares as part of that deal, and has been partnering with Nokia on AI-RAN heavily ever since.

But the chip company has since sold 93.53 million shares between July and September, Nvidia confirmed in the SEC filing.

Nvidia now owns just under 73 million shares in Nokia, with the stake worth around $738.8 million.

The company has supported Nokia's AI-RAN vision, pairing with a number of mobile carriers across the world, while also working towards the 6G era.

The timing of the filing comes amid the high-profile exit of Nvidia's founder, Jensen Huang, last week. Huang resigned after admitting an affair with an executive accused of funneling chips into China, with further affairs since being reported.

Nvidia is currently under the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress in the wake of the scandal, though Nvidia has faced mounting calls to reinstate Huang.

It isn't just Nokia that Nvidia cut its stake in this week. The company also slimmed down its stake in Intel by 25 percent, plus its stake in Synopsys by roughly 10 percent.

However, Nvidia did increase its stake in SpaceX, adding 7.7 million shares, taking its total stake in SpaceX to $19.68 bn. It has more than 130 million shares in the company.
summary: The company sold 93.53 million Nokia shares between July and September, also trims Intel stake, but increases stake in SpaceX
